note: The only differences from the declarations before the TypeScript moves that the public-surface check accepts, each as the one failed assertion of one subject with the old and new value the compiler reports. An entry absorbs nothing else on its subject, and an entry the check no longer needs fails it. These are pair-assertion differences, not the only observable changes: the new augmentation reach is asserted in catalog-examples-types.test.mjs, and new exports are listed in public-surface-inventory.json.

accepted.subject: .:type:DataDiffValues
accepted.reason: Readonly<Record<string, DataDiffValue>> became { readonly [columnId: string]: DataDiffValue }. keyof a string index signature is string | number where the Record alias gave string; mutual assignability and every other key set are unchanged.

accepted.subject: .:type:ResizableSizes
accepted.reason: Readonly<Record<string, number>> became { readonly [panelId: string]: number }, with the same keyof widening.

accepted.subject: .:type:MuxUIValidationErrors
accepted.reason: Readonly<Record<string, string | string[]>> became { readonly [key: string]: string | string[] }, with the same keyof widening.

accepted.subject: .:props:PromptComposer
accepted.reason: PromptComposerProps no longer intersects the form's own defaultValue (string | number | readonly string[]) with the composer's string: the old type was string | (string & readonly string[]), the new one is string. Against unaugmented React, assignment, reading, and JSX accept the same values, and each type is assignable to the other. The old branch string & readonly string[] has no real values, so there the difference shows only where the type is reflected: the readonly keys of its apparent members (number | "length" before, never now), and conditional types over it, where Extract<NonNullable<PromptComposerProps['defaultValue']>, readonly string[]> was string & readonly string[] and is now never. A consumer's augmentation of React's FormHTMLAttributes defaultValue no longer narrows PromptComposer's defaultValue: with defaultValue?: 'draft' augmented, defaultValue="other" was rejected and is now accepted. Keeping the branch would mean loosening the extractor's identity check on owned props.

accepted.subject: .:part:PaymentInput.Root
accepted.reason: PaymentInput.Root no longer intersects the div's own defaultValue (string | number | readonly string[]) with the field's string: the old type was string | (string & readonly string[]), the new one is string. Against unaugmented React, reading, assignment in both directions, JSX and keyof are unchanged, and each type is assignable to the other. The old branch string & readonly string[] has no real values, so the difference shows only where the type is reflected: the readonly keys of its apparent members (number | "length" before, never now), and conditional types over it, where Extract<NonNullable<PaymentInput.Root['defaultValue']>, readonly string[]> was string & readonly string[] and is now never. The equivalence is stated for unaugmented React only: merging a narrower defaultValue into React's HTMLAttributes is itself a compile error (TS2717), so no consumer regression under augmentation is claimed. Keeping the branch would mean loosening the extractor's identity check on owned props.
